edges.description: Recurrent injury, degeneration, and fibrofatty replacement contribute to progressive loss of skeletal muscle function; the pace varies across patients.
Circulating creatine kinase is a marker of skeletal muscle injury in Becker muscular dystrophy. Its level does not directly measure remaining strength and can decline as muscle is replaced by fat.
Proximal weakness is the principal clinical manifestation of the skeletal myopathy.
Pelvic-girdle involvement alters gait as weakness progresses.
Axial muscle weakness can contribute to scoliosis.
Extension of muscle weakness to respiratory muscles can reduce ventilatory capacity.

Cardiac dystrophin dysfunction can lead to progressive ventricular impairment. The exon 45-47 rat model supports progression to cardiomyopathy, while the intervening cellular sequence is not fully established for human Becker disease.
edges.target: Left Ventricular Impairment and Dilated Cardiomyopathy

edges.description: The exon 45-47 rat model shows altered intercalated-disc architecture and protein localization. The contribution of dystrophin quantity versus its altered structure is unresolved.
Reduced LVEF is the clinical readout of ventricular systolic dysfunction.

edges.description: Becker ventricular disease can progress to dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.

nodes.description: ACE inhibitors are first-line medication for established Becker cardiomyopathy in the 2023 French guideline. That guideline recommends specialist discussion of cardioprotective treatment when LVEF is below 50% or MRI shows myocardial fibrosis. It does not recommend prophylactic ACE inhibition for every Becker patient with normal cardiac findings; evidence from Duchenne muscular dystrophy does not establish that indication in Becker muscular dystrophy.

evidence.snippet: Thus, there is no indication to use ACE inhibitors for systematic treatment of BMD patients regardless of cardiac phenotype, such as in Duchenne MD.

nodes.description: In exon 45-47 Becker rats, TMEM65 and connexin-43 are mislocalized and intercalated discs have widened, irregular folds and abnormal contacts with nearby sarcomeres. These findings suggest impaired cardiomyocyte coupling, but no targeted rescue experiment establishes their mediation of ventricular dysfunction. This is model-derived evidence, not a demonstrated universal human cellular lesion.

nodes.description: Cardiac transplantation may be considered for terminal heart failure in selected patients with limited skeletal muscle disability and without severe respiratory failure. Selection requires multidisciplinary assessment. The French guideline generally does not recommend transplantation after loss of ambulation or with significant respiratory failure; ventricular assist devices can be discussed individually in expert centers.

nodes.description: Dystrophin supports muscle membrane stability. In Becker muscular dystrophy, residual protein does not fully prevent contraction-related injury. Exon 45-47 bmx mouse muscle shows increased force loss after eccentric contractions, raised serum creatine kinase, necrotic and inflammatory foci, regeneration, and fibrosis. The severity of individual measurements need not lie uniformly between wild type and dystrophin-null muscle.

nodes.description: Pathogenic variants in DMD alter dystrophin quantity or function. In-frame deletions and duplications are common, but neither reading frame nor variant position alone establishes the Becker phenotype. The Italian cohort included 779 in-frame, 89 out-of-frame, and 35 nonsense variants among 903 genetically characterized patients. Particular exon deletions correlate with clinical outcomes at the group level; substantial variation remains within genotypes and families.

evidence.reference_title: An explanation for the phenotypic differences between patients bearing partial deletions of the DMD locus.
evidence.snippet: Deletions identified in three BMD patients are shown to maintain the translational ORF for amino acids and predict a shorter, lower molecular weight protein.

evidence.reference_title: Natural history of Becker muscular dystrophy: DMD gene mutations predict clinical severity.

The bmx mouse demonstrates reduced cardiac dystrophin and impaired ventricular function; human surveillance must therefore consider the heart even when skeletal weakness is mild.

nodes.description: During exercise, affected muscle may fail to attenuate reflex sympathetic vasoconstriction, causing functional ischemia under experimental conditions. This abnormality is associated with nNOS membrane localization but is not present in every Becker patient. Acute tadalafil or nitrate studies demonstrate reversibility of the vascular response; its contribution to chronic weakness or disease progression remains unresolved. Reduced local NO-cGMP signaling is supported by the localization findings and pharmacological rescue rather than by a direct assay of intracellular cGMP in these patients.

evidence.snippet: The key finding of our study is that tadalafil alleviated microvascular ischemia and fully restored blood flow regulation in eight of nine BMD patients who lacked sympatholysis when given placebo.

nodes.description: Sevasemten inhibits fast skeletal muscle myosin ATPase to reduce injurious contraction. A short phase 1 Becker cohort comprised five treated patients and two placebo recipients; muscle-injury biomarkers decreased but the study was too small and short to establish clinical efficacy. In a later uncontrolled 12-person study, biomarkers remained reduced and functional measures were stable over two years. These observations support investigation, not a proven treatment effect. The completed CANYON/GRAND CANYON registry had no posted results at the September 2026 review.

nodes.description: Dystrophin serves as a scaffold for sarcolemmal nNOS. Some Becker variants reduce or abolish membrane nNOS localization; other variants retain it. In a biopsy-linked human series, nNOS staining was absent in seven patients and present in six. Total nNOS abundance and residual localization also vary, including between relatives with the same splice variant.

nodes.description: Residual dystrophin distinguishes the Becker phenotype from severe dystrophin deficiency, but its abundance and function vary. Internally deleted dystrophin is a common outcome, not the only one. In bmx mice with deletion of Dmd exons 45-47, skeletal and cardiac dystrophin protein is reduced despite preserved transcript abundance. Sarcolemmal nNOS localization is lost and alpha-sarcoglycan localization is reduced in this model; these allele-specific observations should not be assumed for every Becker variant.

nodes.description: In a study of 12 Becker patients with exon 45-55 deletions, cytosolic nitric oxide production correlated with RyR1 hypernitrosylation and calstabin-1 dissociation. These findings implicate altered regulation of the sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium-release complex. The association does not establish measured calcium leak or its causal contribution across Becker genotypes.

evidence.snippet: Cytosolic NO production correlated with both hypernitrosylation of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium-release-channel ryanodine receptor type-1 (RyR1) and release of calstabin-1, a central hub of Ca(2+) signaling and contraction in muscle.

nodes.description: Proximal weakness and mobility loss progress at variable rates. In the retrospective Italian cohort, 111 of 822 patients with available ambulation information had lost walking ability at assessment. The Kaplan-Meier median age at loss of ambulation was 69 years, whereas the observed mean age among those who had already lost ambulation was 35.3 years. These are different statistics; neither describes an inevitable course for an individual. Respiratory decline can become clinically important, especially after loss of ambulation, and warrants surveillance.
